events.description: Enrolled in a part-time master's in educational leadership after fourteen years teaching geography.
Moved from the corner seat to the front staffroom table, ending his position as last to hear about changes.
Father had a minor stroke in Manisa; Deniz reached the hospital four hours ahead of him.
Drove down the same night and waited in the hospital corridor until the morning shift arrived.
Booked a recurring Thursday two-hour university library slot and entered it in the school calendar under his own name.
Bulent observed the year eleven lesson and told the deputy that written feedback had already been sent.
Asked Bulent twice for the observation notes in writing; both requests were deferred.
Replaced the why-are-you-absent question with a question about Emre's first ten morning minutes.
Kerem began inviting him on Saturday coast photography walks; invitations deferred for months.
Split the caregiving week with Deniz into named days, ending the middle-of-the-night phone calls.
Sent a written account of the observation to the union representative; no response followed.
Held the first meeting with Emre's mother about the attendance referral.
Recorded a chapter aloud and replayed it while driving, exposing the unclear passages Selin had flagged.
Father discharged; medication times posted inside the kitchen cupboard door shared with Deniz.
Offered and accepted the acting head of year nine role from September, one year in the first instance.
Secured the extra teaching-free period in writing before accepting; it appeared in the September timetable.
Restarted Saturday coast walks with his mother's camera, six consecutive weekends.
Moved Emre to a front seat by the window with no observable change in attendance.
March re-observation with the deputy present; written notes arrived the following day and the appraisal closed.
Sent Selin the complete dissertation draft; verdict still outstanding.

dialogue.text: I'm Yusuf, forty-one, and I have taught geography in the same secondary school for fourteen years. Last month I enrolled in a part-time master's in educational leadership, and the first assignment has been open on my screen for nine days without a paragraph in it.
Fourteen years of knowing exactly what you're doing, and now a blank page that refuses to behave. What happens when you sit down to it?
I plan the lesson for tomorrow instead. Every single time. Teaching is the thing I can do well, so my hands go there on their own.
The competent task keeps outbidding the uncomfortable one. That is not laziness — it's a very reasonable retreat toward the ground where you're already good.

dialogue.text: Something small but constant: I'm the only male teacher in the geography department, and I am always the last one to hear anything. Timetable changes, trip dates, meeting rooms — I find out from the noticeboard.
Being informed last, repeatedly, is its own quiet message about where you sit in the room.

So I made myself a rule and started sitting at the front table in the staffroom instead of my usual corner by the window, and within a fortnight people were telling me about changes before the noticeboard did.
You moved three metres and changed who talks to you. Information travels by proximity more than anyone likes to admit.

dialogue.text: My father collapsed on Tuesday. A stroke, a small one they keep saying. I teach in Izmir and my parents are two hours down the road in Manisa, so my sister Deniz was at the hospital four hours before I was.
Four hours behind, on a road you couldn't make go any faster. That gap tends to sit heavier than it deserves to.
I drove down the same night and sat in that corridor until the morning shift came on, and I still have no idea whether that helped anybody or just kept me from thinking.
Sometimes both at once. A corridor at three in the morning is not a place where usefulness is measurable.
He has run the same hardware shop in Manisa since he was twenty-six, and he was asking about the delivery van before the doctors had finished their sentence.
Forty years of opening that shop doesn't switch off because a doctor says so. The van is how he checks he's still himself.

dialogue.text: Back to the master's. My whole reading list is in English, and I was born and schooled in Turkey, so here is what I have noticed: the chapters only stay with me when I write the summary in my own language first and translate it afterwards.
Your understanding forms in one language and gets exported to the other. Translating last keeps the thinking where it actually happens.
The other thing I did was book a two-hour slot in the university library every Thursday and put it in the school calendar under my own name, and not one person has taken those hours off me since.
A named booking is much harder to erase than an intention. The calendar defends it for you now.
One thing about how you answer me — if I ask you something factual, give me the short version. I read all day for work; I don't need an essay back.
Short it is, from here on.

dialogue.text: Bulent, our department head, observed my year eleven lesson three weeks ago. He told the deputy he had sent me written feedback the same week. I have never received a single line from him in writing, and my inbox agrees with me.
Two accounts of the same three weeks, and his reached the deputy first. That is an awkward place to be arguing from.
I have asked him twice now to put the observation notes in writing, and both times he said he would get to it.
Twice asked, twice deferred. The delay is doing work for him whether or not that's deliberate.

dialogue.text: There is a boy in my tutor group, Emre, whose attendance has fallen off a cliff. Every adult in that building has asked him why he is not in school, and every adult gets the same shrug.
He has heard the question so often it has stopped being a question. The shrug is the only answer left that costs him nothing.
So on Friday I stopped asking why he was absent and asked him what the first ten minutes of his morning look like, and he talked for a quarter of an hour without stopping.
You asked about the mornings instead of the absence, and suddenly there was nothing to defend. Fifteen minutes from a shrugger is a lot.
Separately, Kerem from the history department keeps trying to drag me out on Saturday photography walks along the coast. I keep telling him next week.
Next week has been doing heavy lifting for a while now. He seems willing to keep asking, at least.

And honestly, most evenings I am not looking for anything to be fixed. Just let me say it out and don't hand me things to do.
Understood. I'll listen and leave the doing alone unless you ask for it.

dialogue.text: I have worked out that there are two different tirednesses in this job. Teaching six lessons leaves me empty but calm; the hour before meeting Emre's mother leaves me wired and useless, and the two need completely different evenings.
Empty and calm versus wired and useless. Those really are two different states wearing the same word.
His family moved between three districts last year, which nobody at school seems to have on file anywhere.
Three districts in a year, and the file says nothing. The record is describing a different child than the one in front of you.

dialogue.text: A trick out of pure desperation: I read the whole chapter out loud into my phone and played it back on the drive home, and the sentences that made no sense were obvious inside the first minute.
Your ear caught in sixty seconds what your eye had skimmed past for weeks. Reading aloud is unforgiving in the useful way.
Selin, my supervisor, had written unclear argument four times in the margin and I genuinely could not see it on the page.
You had read it too many times to hear it. The car gave you a stranger's ears for half an hour.

An empty file with a deadline attached. The closing date is doing the pressuring that he never had to.

Different world at home. My father's discharge papers arrived on Saturday and I did not try to keep any of it in my head. The medication times went on the inside of the kitchen cupboard door, where Deniz and I both look every single morning. Neither of us has missed one since.
You put the information where the two of you already were, instead of asking your memory to be somewhere new. That is a good deal quieter than a reminder app.

One year, with an exit written into it. That is a serious step and a reversible one, which is rarer than it sounds.
Before I said yes I asked the deputy head to put the extra teaching-free period in writing, and it turned up in the September timetable exactly as agreed.
You made the condition concrete before accepting, and the timetable honoured it. Verbal versions of that promise usually evaporate in August.

dialogue.text: I changed how I go to Selin. Instead of sending the whole chapter I sent her one specific question about the sampling, and she replied inside a day for the first time in a year.
A narrow question is answerable between meetings. A whole chapter needs a free afternoon she never has.
There is a clock on this as well — the department covers half the tuition only if I submit inside four years.
So the deadline has a price tag attached, not just a date. That changes how the last year has to be spent.
My father is walking to the shop and back most days now, though Deniz still does the Tuesday drive.
From a corridor at three in the morning to the walk to the shop. That is a long way in a year and a half.
